question: Which word is a collective noun?
why: A herd is a group of animals taken as one.

question: In 'Her honesty impressed the teacher', which word is an abstract noun?
why: Honesty is a quality you cannot touch.

question: What is the plural of 'child'?
why: Child has an irregular plural.

question: What is the plural of 'knife'?
why: Nouns ending in -fe change to -ves.

question: Meera is my best friend. ___ lives near my house. Choose the pronoun.
why: Meera is one girl, so we use 'She'.

question: Replace the noun in 'The boys played cricket' with a pronoun.
why: 'The boys' is plural and third person, so 'They'.

question: Which sentence has a collective noun?
c: A swarm of bees settled on the tree.
why: Swarm names a group of bees.

question: Which is the abstract noun in 'The villagers admired Anil's courage during the flood'?
why: Courage is a quality; the others are things or people.

question: Which pair is correctly matched as singular and plural?
why: Mouse and goose are irregular; wolf makes wolves; sheep stays sheep.

question: What are the plurals of 'baby' and 'monkey'?
why: Consonant + y becomes -ies; vowel + y just adds -s.

question: Ravi and I went to the market. ___ bought mangoes. Choose the pronoun.
why: 'Ravi and I' is the subject, so we use 'We'.

question: The teacher gave the prize to Neha and ___. Choose the correct word.
why: After 'to' we need the object form 'me'.

question: In 'Kabir showed kindness to the dog', the nouns Kabir, kindness and dog are respectively:
why: Kabir names a person, kindness is a quality, dog is a general name.

question: Which noun is used only in the plural form?
why: Scissors is always plural in form.

question: Which sentence has all the plurals correct?
a: The two mans carried three boxes of tomatoes.
b: The two men carried three boxs of tomatoes.
c: The two men carried three boxes of tomatoes.
d: The two mens carried three boxes of tomatos.
why: Man becomes men; box takes -es; tomato takes -es.

question: Which noun has the same form in singular and plural?
why: Deer is both one deer and many deer.

question: The little boy hurt ___ while climbing the wall. Choose the pronoun.
why: A reflexive pronoun must match the boy: himself.

question: Which sentence uses the possessive pronoun correctly?
a: This pen is my, not your.
b: This pen is mine, not yours.
c: This pen is me, not you.
d: This pen is mine, not your.
why: Mine and yours stand alone without a noun after them.

question: Choose the article: ___ apple a day keeps the doctor away.
why: Apple starts with a vowel sound, so 'an'.

question: Choose the article: She bought ___ umbrella.
why: Umbrella begins with a vowel sound /u/ as in 'up'.

question: Fill in: I have ___ pencils in my box. (a small number, countable)
why: Few is used with countable plural nouns.

question: Fill in: There is ___ milk in the glass. (not full)
why: Some fits an uncountable noun like milk.

question: Choose the demonstrative: ___ book here on my desk is new.
why: 'Here' and one book mean 'This'.

question: Choose the word: Aman lost ___ bag yesterday.
why: 'His' is the possessive that goes before a noun.

question: Choose the article: He is ___ honest boy.
why: Honest starts with a vowel sound because h is silent.

question: Choose the article: Ravi is ___ European student.
why: European begins with a 'y' sound, a consonant sound.

question: Which sentence is correct?
why: Water is uncountable, so 'a little'.

question: Which sentence is correct?
why: Mangoes are countable, so 'many'.

question: Fill in: ___ birds over there are sparrows.
why: Far and plural means 'Those'.

question: Fill in: The girls forgot ___ lunch boxes.
why: 'Their' shows the girls own the boxes.

question: Which sentence needs 'the' in the blank? ___ Ganga is a holy river.
why: Names of rivers take 'the'.

question: Choose the correct sentence.
c: The sun rises in a east.
d: The sun rises in the east.
why: Unique things like the sun take 'the', and 'the east' too.

question: Which sentence uses 'little' correctly to mean 'almost none'?
a: There is little hope of rain today.
b: There is a little hope of rain today.
c: There are little hopes of rain.
d: There is few hope of rain today.
why: 'Little' without 'a' is negative: hardly any.

question: Which sentence uses 'few' to mean 'some, enough'?
a: Few guests arrived early, so we had help.
b: A few guests arrived early, so we started.
why: 'A few' is positive: some.

question: Choose the correct sentence.
a: Two those red balls are mine.
b: Red two those balls are mine.
c: Those two red balls are mine.
d: Those red two ball are mine.
why: Determiners such as 'those' come before numbers and adjectives.

question: Which sentence has the article error?
why: University starts with a 'yoo' sound so 'a' is needed.

question: Choose the correct verb: She ___ to school every day.
why: Third person singular takes -es in simple present.

question: Choose the past form: Yesterday, we ___ to the park.
why: Go has an irregular past: went.

question: Choose the correct form: Birds ___ in the sky now.
why: Plural subject and 'now' need 'are flying'.

question: Choose the correct form: He ___ his homework right now.
why: 'Right now' needs present continuous with 'is'.

question: Choose the correct form: Tomorrow I ___ my grandmother.
why: Tomorrow shows future, so 'will visit'.

question: Which sentence is in the future tense?
why: 'Will play' marks the future.

question: Choose the correct form: My father ___ tea every morning.
why: Habit in the present; he takes -s.

question: Choose the correct form: She ___ her room yesterday.
why: Yesterday needs simple past.

question: Choose the correct form: The children ___ when the teacher came in.
why: Past continuous with plural subject: were talking.

question: Choose the correct form: I ___ a letter when the lights went out.
why: An action in progress in the past uses 'was writing'.

question: Choose the correct form: Next week, Priya ___ to Jaipur.
why: 'Next week' shows the future.

question: Choose the correct form: Do you know if it ___ tomorrow?
why: A future event needs 'will rain'.

question: Which sentence is correct?
a: He did not go to school yesterday.
b: He did not went to school yesterday.
c: He not went to school yesterday.
d: He did not goes to school yesterday.
why: After 'did not' use the base verb: go.

question: Which sentence is correct?
why: After 'does' use the base verb: play.

question: Which sentence is correct?
a: I was read while my sister cooked.
b: I read while my sister was cook.
c: I was reading while my sister was cooking.
d: I am reading while my sister was cooking.
why: Two actions going on together in the past use past continuous.

question: Which sentence has the verb tense error?
a: Yesterday I went to the market.
b: Tomorrow I will go to the market.
c: Now I am going to the market.
d: Yesterday I will go to the market.
why: 'Yesterday' cannot be used with 'will go'.

question: Which sentence is correct?
a: The sun rises in the east.
b: The sun rose in the east every day.
c: The sun is rise in the east.
d: The sun rising in the east.
why: General truths use the simple present.

question: Which sentence is correct?
a: If it will rain tomorrow, we will stay home.
b: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay home.
c: If it rained tomorrow, we stay home.
d: If it rains tomorrow, we stayed home.
why: After 'if' we use present, not 'will', for a future condition.

question: Choose the preposition: The cat is sleeping ___ the table.
why: Under shows place; the others are not prepositions of place.

question: Choose the preposition: School starts ___ 8 o'clock.
why: Use 'at' with a clock time.

question: Choose the correct word: Mohan was born ___ 2014.
why: Use 'in' with years.

question: Choose the correct word: We play cricket ___ Sundays.
why: Use 'on' with days.

question: Choose the conjunction: I like tea ___ coffee.
why: 'And' joins two similar things.

question: Choose the conjunction: She was tired, ___ she kept walking.
why: 'But' shows contrast.

question: Choose the correct word: The bird flew ___ the window.
why: Through shows movement from one side to the other.

question: Choose the correct word: She is good ___ painting.
why: 'Good at' is the fixed phrase.

question: Choose the correct word: I am afraid ___ dogs.
why: 'Afraid of' is the right phrase.

question: Choose the correct word: He is interested ___ music.
why: 'Interested in' is correct.

question: Choose the conjunction: Hurry up, ___ you will miss the bus.
why: 'Or' warns of what happens otherwise.

question: Choose the conjunction: He stayed home ___ he was ill.
why: 'Because' gives the reason.

question: Choose the correct word: The books were divided ___ the three girls.
why: Use 'among' for more than two.

question: Choose the correct word: The ball rolled ___ the two chairs.
why: Between is used for two.

question: Choose the correct word: He has lived here ___ 2019.
why: 'Since' goes with a starting point in time.

question: Choose the correct word: She has been waiting ___ two hours.
why: 'For' goes with a length of time.

question: Choose the conjunction: ___ it was raining, we went out to play.
why: Although shows the surprising contrast.

question: Choose the conjunction: You cannot enter ___ you show your ticket.
why: 'Unless' means 'if not'.

question: Which word is an adjective in 'The red kite flew high'?
why: Red describes the kite.

question: Choose the comparative: Ria is ___ than Sia. (tall)
why: Add -er to short adjectives to compare two.

question: Choose the adverb: She sings sweetly.
why: Sweetly tells how she sings.

question: Choose the correct word: He runs ___. (quick)
why: A verb is described by an adverb.

question: Choose the superlative: Mount Everest is the ___ mountain. (high)
why: The superlative of high is highest.

question: Choose the correct word: This box is ___ than that one. (heavy)
why: Change y to i and add -er.

question: Choose the correct word: Of all the boys, Dev is the ___. (good)
why: Good - better - best is irregular.

question: Choose the correct word: This story is ___ than that one. (interesting)
why: Long adjectives take 'more'.

question: Which word is an adverb of time? 'We will leave soon.'
why: Soon tells when.

question: Which word is an adverb of place? 'The children played outside.'
why: Outside tells where.

question: Choose the correct word: She answered the question ___. (correct)
why: An adverb describes how she answered.

question: Choose the correct word: She is the ___ girl in the class. (young)
why: Three or more things need superlative.

question: Choose the correct word: He is ___ than his brother. (clever)
why: Two persons: comparative; clever takes -er.

question: Which sentence is correct?
a: She is the beautifulest girl here.
b: She is the most beautiful girl here.
c: She is more beautiful girl here.
why: Long adjectives take most for the superlative.

question: Which sentence is correct?
a: He did good in the test.
b: He did goodly in the test.
c: He did well in the test.
d: He did best in the test, than me.
why: 'Well' is the adverb; 'good' is an adjective.

question: Which sentence has an adverb modifying an adjective?
why: 'Very' describes the adjective 'hot'.

question: Which sentence is correct?
a: This is the less expensive of the two bags.
b: This is the least expensive of the two bags.
c: This is the less expensive from the two bags.
why: With two, we use the comparative: less.

question: Choose the correct sentence.
why: 'Late' is the adverb meaning not on time; 'lately' means recently.

question: In 'my sister lives in jaipur.' which word needs a capital letter?
why: Names of places are proper nouns and begin with a capital.

question: Which sentence needs a question mark?
why: It is a question.

question: Which sentence is an exclamatory sentence?
why: It shows sudden strong feeling.

question: Which is a command?
why: A command tells someone to do something.

question: Choose the correct sentence.
why: Apostrophe replaces the o in 'do not'.

question: Which sentence has a comma used correctly?
a: I bought, apples bananas and grapes.
b: I bought apples bananas, and, grapes.
c: I, bought apples bananas and grapes.
d: I bought apples, bananas and grapes.
why: Commas separate items in a list.

question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
why: Comma comes after the opening 'Yes'.

question: Choose the correct apostrophe: This is ___ pen.
why: The apostrophe + s shows possession.

question: Where does the comma go? 'After lunch we played cricket'.
why: A comma follows an opening phrase.

question: Which sentence needs an exclamation mark?
why: It shows excitement.

question: Which is an interrogative sentence?
why: It asks a question.

question: Which sentence is declarative?
a: Is the Taj Mahal in Agra?
b: The Taj Mahal is in Agra.
d: How grand the Taj Mahal is!
why: It states a fact.

question: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
b: Mother said, please wash your hands.
d: Mother said: Please, wash your hands.
why: Direct speech needs a comma, quotation marks and a capital letter inside.

question: Which uses 'its' and 'it's' correctly?
a: Its raining, and the dog is in it's kennel.
b: It's raining, and the dog is in it's kennel.
c: Its raining, and the dog is in its' kennel.
d: It's raining, and the dog is in its kennel.
why: It's = it is; its = belonging to it.

question: Many boys left bags on the bench. Which sentence is correct?
a: The boys' bags are on the bench.
b: The boy's bags are on the bench.
c: The boys bags' are on the bench.
d: The boys's bags are on the bench.
why: Plural boys takes only an apostrophe after the s.

question: Which sentence has the commas right?
a: Ria my cousin, is a doctor.
b: Ria, my cousin, is a doctor.
c: Ria, my cousin is, a doctor.
d: Ria my, cousin is a doctor.
why: Commas set off extra information.

question: Which is the correct imperative sentence?
a: Will you pass the salt please.
why: It gives a polite command.

question: Which sentence is exclamatory and correctly punctuated?
why: An exclamation ends with !, and 'How tall ... is' keeps the statement order.

question: Choose the synonym of 'big'.
why: Large means big.

question: Choose the synonym of 'happy'.
why: Glad is close in meaning to happy.

question: Choose the antonym of 'hot'.
why: Cold is the opposite of hot.

question: Choose the antonym of 'early'.
why: Late is the opposite of early.

question: Choose the correct word: I can ___ the bell. (hear/here)
why: Hear is what ears do.

question: Choose the correct word: Come ___ and sit. (hear/here)
why: 'Here' means in this place.

question: Choose the synonym of 'begin'.
why: Start means begin.

question: Choose the synonym of 'brave'.
why: Courageous means brave.

question: Choose the antonym of 'ancient'.
why: Modern is the opposite of ancient.

question: Choose the antonym of 'generous'.
why: Stingy means unwilling to give.

question: Choose the right word: The ___ of the cake was delicious. (piece/peace)
why: Piece means a part; peace is calm.

question: Choose the right word: I like to ___ a book every week. (read/red)
why: Read is the verb; red is a colour.

question: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'rapid'.
why: Swift means fast.

question: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'enormous'.
why: Gigantic means very large.

question: Choose the antonym of 'victory'.
why: Defeat is the opposite of victory.

question: Choose the antonym of 'expand'.
why: Shrink is the opposite of expand.

question: Choose the correct sentence.
a: The principal gave a speech about good principles.
b: The principle gave a speech about good principals.
c: The principal gave a speech about good principals.
d: The principle gave a speech about good principles.
why: Principal = head; principle = rule.

question: Choose the correct sentence.
a: Please except this gift from us.
b: Please accept this gift from us.
c: Please expect this gift from us.
d: Please excepting this gift from us.
why: Accept means to receive; except means 'other than'.
